newsitem.title: CANADA: Tobacco bill progresses through Canadian House.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco bill progresses through Canadian House.

text.p: A government bill to restrict tobacco advertising and sponsorships passed another hurdle late on Tuesday and will almost certainly be approved by the House of Commons on Thursday night.

An official at the House, Parliament's elected chamber, approved the bill at "report stage" on Tuesday and is slated to have a final vote late on Thursday. It will then proceed to the Senate, the unelected upper chamber.
The bill would ban tobacco ads through broadcasting or billboards, ban tobacco sales through vending machines and restrict the use of tobacco brand names in sponsored events.
The last provision has created a storm in Quebec, home to cultural and sporting events which could receive less funding from tobacco companies.
The government has agreed to delay implementing the sponsorship rules until October 1998, allowing two more summers of unrestricted tobacco sponsorship.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain.

The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, owned by Swiss luxury goods holding company Cie Financiere Richmont AG, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Third place holder RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
